title: docs(audits): mark the 2026-06 react-tier dogfood audit superseded on three points
body:
Fixes #10284

`docs/audits/2026-06-react-tier-authoring-dogfood.md` is cited as the trustworthy record of what a react-tier author actually sees — three separate consumers reached for it in one dispatch round — and three of its load-bearing claims have rotted. This adds a dated **superseded on three points** header and changes nothing else in the file.

## Why a header rather than a refreshed body

An audit is a dated record of what someone actually observed, and that is where its authority comes from. Rewriting the body to match August behaviour would destroy the record and create a worse hazard than the one being fixed: a document titled *2026-06* that describes behaviour from two months later is misleading in a way no reader can detect. The conclusion — contract → author → gate composes into a working loop — still holds; only the evidence rotted, so the evidence is what gets marked.

Shape precedent: ADR-0080's `Amendment (2026-06-30 — ADR-0065 styling correction)` blockquote, and the `⚠️ Correction (2026-08-01, #4472)` header this same directory already carries on `2026-06-react-blocks-conformance.md`.

Re-running the full dogfood loop would produce a *new* audit — different work from repairing this one's citations, and it should be its own card.

## The three, re-derived at `b05a543654`

**1. The example page's path moved.** `ls` on the cited path fails; `find . -name '*renewals*'` returns exactly `./examples/app-showcase/src/ui/pages/renewals-pipeline.page.ts`. (The issue says the path is stated twice; measured, the *fully-qualified* path appears once, at line 16 — line 55 cites the bare basename, which is still correct. The header corrects the one citation.)

**2. The `record:*` family is out of the react tier.** `REACT_RECORD_BLOCK_ALTERNATIVES` and the ledger above it in `packages/spec/src/ui/react-blocks.ts` record the withdrawal, and `grep -n '^## '` on the generated contract `skills/objectstack-ui/references/react-blocks.md` now returns four blocks — `<ObjectForm>`, `<ListView>`, `<ObjectChart>`, `<Block>` — and no `Record*`. Measured, not inferred: putting `<RecordHighlights objectName recordId>` back on the renewals page and running the built CLI exits 1 with `rule: react-block-needs-record-context`. The page was restored byte-for-byte afterwards; the diff here is one file.

**3. The quoted CLI banners exist nowhere.** `grep -rn "React-source page"` over the tree returns only the audit's own two lines. `validateReactPageProps` is no longer a hand-wired `os validate` step with its own banner — it joined the shared reference-integrity suite (`packages/lint/src/reference-integrity-suite.ts`) inside the author-time rule registry, so `os validate` / `os lint` / `os build` all reach it and it reports under the registry's single banner.

The replacement text is **real output captured from the CLI built at this revision** against `examples/app-showcase`, not a paraphrase and not copied from the issue: the pass run (`✓ Validation passed (1302ms)`, exit 0) and the fail run with the same two injected mistakes (`✗ Author-time rules failed (1 issue)` … `rule: react-prop-missing-required  at pages[27].source`, exit 1).

**A fourth drift fell out of capturing that.** The audit's failure block shows the `onSucces` typo warning and the missing-`objectName` error together; they never render in one run. The error gate exits before advisories are rendered, so with both mistakes injected the warning is not printed at all. It still exists and is worded exactly as the audit has it — with *only* the typo injected it appears in the advisory list after the pass banner, exit 0. The severity split the audit describes is intact; the interleaving is not. Folded into correction 3 since it is the same quoted block.

**On `pages[29]` → `pages[27]`:** agreed it is not worth pinning, and the real output above carries the current index anyway. The header notes it in one clause — framed as positional drift that was never a stable citation — precisely so the next reader does not re-file it as rot.

## Verification

Gate families derived at the final commit `b4bed7c616` with `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` (no paths passed — the script derives its own change set from the merge base). All seven run under `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh`, exit codes captured before any pipe, verdicts quoted from each gate's own output:

| gate | exit | its own verdict line |
|---|---|---|
| `check:doc-authoring` | 0 | `✓ doc authoring guard: 389 files clean — no bare metadata literals.` |
| `check:doc-formula-expressions` | 0 | `✓ check:doc-formula-expressions: 22 record-scoped formula example(s) across 416 files / 1443 TS blocks judged clean` |
| `check:empty-state` | 0 | `✓ all classified (1 closed, 2 open, 4 output, 9 scope)` |
| `check:liveness` | 0 | `✓ every governed-type property at the walk's one-level granularity is classified …` |
| `check:strictness-ledger` | 0 | `✓ strictness ledger: 61 file(s) across 5 triaged director(ies) …` |
| `check:variant-docs` | 0 | `✓ variant/doc gate: 18 discriminated union(s) — 8 governed, 10 exempt.` |
| `check:nul-bytes` | 0 | `check-nul-bytes: OK (scanned 6249 text file(s) … no raw ASCII control bytes).` |

The dispatch's guesses `check:doc-anchors` and `check:docs-audit-scope` are not gate families in this tree; the derivation named the six above instead, plus `check:nul-bytes` for any edit.

Note on `check:doc-authoring`: it is green, and its own self-test states `docs/{audits,handoff,plans}` are outside its walk — a deliberate, self-documented over-claim in its declared population, not a gap this PR introduces.

**No ablation applies** — docs-only, no guard under test. The CLI runs above are output captures, not ablations; each mutation was confirmed on disk by anchored `grep -c` on both the injected and the removed text plus the real diff hunks, and each restore was confirmed by an empty `git status --porcelain`.

Docs-only and publishes nothing, so no changeset; `skip-changeset` applied.
